subject: Usage anomaly and renewal options — root cause + suggested paths
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Gomez <sofia.gomez@latticehealth.com>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@latticehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage anomaly and renewal options — root cause + suggested paths

Hi Sofia + Luis,

Following up on our renewal cadence — we pulled a fresh usage/latency report for April and noticed a ~42% token spend increase vs. forecast for the last 30 days which is putting you outside the run-rate used for the renewal tiers. I dug into the traces and have a preliminary read:

- There was a sustained increase in system-generated context tokens from the recent feature rollout (longer system prompts + richer metadata).
- A subset of high-concurrency endpoints is experiencing elevated response latencies which caused client retries and a small percent of duplicated requests (see attached latency-samples-apr-2028.png).
- Model mix shifted to the larger variant for certain QA flows on the 14th after your internal A/B test.

I know the renewal window is coming up. Suggested next steps so we can keep your experience predictable and control unit economics:

1) Short term (immediate): grant a one-month burst credit and bump burst capacity while we triage; we can apply a usage credit to April overage as a one-time gesture.
2) Medium term (30 days): enable prefix caching for the long system prompts + route that flow to a cheaper model variant during off-peak hours.
3) Renewal options: either keep current term and add a 20% headroom commit, or move to a tiered commit that matches peak days with an auto-burst fallback.

I've attached a token-spend summary and a short options PDF with back-of-envelope pricing. Ben / Vivek — can you review the proposed commit tiers in the attachment and flag any pricing/CSP concerns?

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call this week to walk through the data. What works for you?

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments:
- 2028-04-token-spend-summary.csv (csv)
- latency-samples-apr-2028.png (image/png)
- proposed-commit-options.pdf (pdf)

----

From: Sofia Gomez <sofia.gomez@latticehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@latticehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 3 May 2028 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage anomaly and renewal options — root cause + suggested paths

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for doing the deep dive — this aligns with what our infra team sees. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The QA A/B test on the 14th intentionally switched a subset to the larger model for higher fidelity responses; we expected some lift but not this magnitude.
- We did roll a richer system prompt on the 10th to improve summarization quality.
- We can run a short rollback to the previous prompt tonight if that helps.

We are open to the one-month burst credit while you investigate. For renewal, we prefer a tiered commit that avoids over-committing but protects us from spikes (we typically see predictable spikes on the 1st and 15th of the month).

Call wise — Thursday 11am PT works for Sophia, Friday morning for Luis. Could you propose two slots?

Best,
Sofia
Product Ops Manager | Lattice Health
sofia.gomez@latticehealth.com

----

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sofia Gomez <sofia.gomez@latticehealth.com>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@latticehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 3 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage anomaly and renewal options — root cause + suggested paths

Marissa — quick pricing read:

- If we do a one-month burst credit covering 50% of the April delta, we reduce churn risk and keep the renewal talks open. Estimated credit: $12,400 (see attached spreadsheet).
- Tiered commit: propose a baseline commit at 80% of current run-rate + two auto-burst bands (100–150% at a higher unit price). This keeps base pricing favorable while providing headroom.
- Also recommend a 6-month pilot for prefix caching on the long prompts — should cut token usage by ~18–25% for that flow.

I'll prepare a short amendment doc we can sign (DocuSign) that puts the burst credit and tiered commit in place as a short-term addendum.

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com

Attachment referenced: pricing-workup-apr-overage.xlsx (xlsx)

----

From: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@latticehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Gomez <sofia.gomez@latticehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 4 May 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage anomaly and renewal options — root cause + suggested paths

Thanks Ben — we appreciate the flexible structures. Two quick asks from procurement:

1) Can the amendment include a 'true-up' clause that allows us to reconcile committed vs actual quarterly?
2) Can you outline SLA credit mechanics if latencies exceed the agreed SLOs during the pilot?

If you can send a draft amendment and quick call, we can get legal eyes on it before the renewal deadline (20 May).

Cheers,
Luis
Head of Procurement | Lattice Health
luis.ortega@latticehealth.com

----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Gomez <sofia.gomez@latticehealth.com>, Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@latticehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 6 May 2028 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage anomaly and renewal options — root cause + suggested paths

Thanks everyone — quick recap and next steps:

- Redwood will:
  - Apply a one-time credit covering 50% of the April overage (credit memo to appear on next invoice).
  - Prepare a short amendment with: baseline commit at 80% run-rate; two burst bands (100% and 150%) with stepped unit prices; a quarterly true-up clause.
  - Enable prefix caching pilot for 6 months on the identified flows; SRE will provide SLO monitoring and an SLA credit table for the pilot.
- Lattice Health will:
  - Decide whether to roll back the richer system prompt tonight (Sofia), and confirm which endpoints to route to cheaper variants.
  - Share legal contact for quick review.
- Action items / meetings:
  - Draft amendment (Ben) — due Wed 8 May EOD.
  - SLA credit table & monitoring plan (Vivek) — due Thu 9 May EOD.
  - Call to discuss amendment: Thu 9 May 10:00 AM PT / Fri 10 May 9:00 AM PT (please confirm).

I'll send calendar invites once you confirm a slot. Thanks again for the quick coordination — goal is to keep Lattice's apps stable and keep renewal straightforward.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments (sent in thread):
- 2028-04-token-spend-summary.csv
- latency-samples-apr-2028.png
- proposed-commit-options.pdf
